published_prior_art.cite: Wongkew1993 gives upper tube-volume bounds; PhongSturm2000 supplies algebraic-integral machinery, not a decidable original-coordinate normal-link certificate.
deChaisemartinDHa2025 supplies the distributed-lag Moore--Penrose setup; PhongSturm2000 and ConcaEtAl2018 supply ingredients but not this target-specific causal tail law.
No checked source computes the stated positive codimension-two Hankel-tail constants for both coordinates at the alternating history.
GrahamPowell2012 and SasakiUra2026 establish trimmed/bias-corrected inference in related random-coefficient panels, not exact fixed-signature minimax risk plus honest expected-length equivalence.
deChaisemartinDHa2025 supplies the finite-support root-G endpoint and GrahamPowell2012 supplies the uncorrected scalar N^{-2/3} balance.
SasakiUra2026 gives scalar slow-mover bias reduction and inference, not multi-lag adaptation across certified Hankel strata with an adaptation lower bound.

soundness_flags.label: def:invariant-indices
soundness_flags.one_line: “Largest tied-face logarithmic multiplicity” and its frontier analogue are not defined by a mathematical rule, so the claimed exact logarithmic powers and rates are presently ambiguous.

soundness_flags.label: def:boundary-extension and def:oracle-estimator
soundness_flags.one_line: The “lexicographically nearest resolved point” lacks a specified metric, chart lift, and cross-chart selection rule, leaving the extension and hence the estimator/bias envelope undefined.

soundness_flags.label: ass:frontier-holder
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited SasakiUra2022 condition concerns smoothness for a scalar ratio numerator/denominator problem, not isotropic Hölder regularity after a frozen resolution atlas; retag this as novel and justify its applicability, or state a directly supported primitive condition.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the distributed-lag equation and Moore--Penrose/projector objects, identifies by truncation when needed, and gives a root-G finite-support plug-in estimator.
For T=p, Theorem 2.1 gives a sqrt(Nh_N) Gaussian limit, and equation (29) gives an MSE-optimal bandwidth proportional to N^{-1/3}.

source_verification_receipts.version: Econometric Theory first-view PDF, published online 7 January 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies correlated random-coefficient panels with stayers/slow movers, higher-order bias reduction, and inference; its main analysis is T=p with an extension to T>p.

source_verification_receipts.locator: publisher abstract and bibliographic record, pp. 66–112
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited article concerns moments E[B/A] and correction of trimming bias under smoothness of the joint distribution of scalar ratio components A and B; it does not state the proposal's frozen-atlas chartwise Hölder condition.
The paper develops algebraic estimates for numerator--denominator integrals and gives distribution-function consequences, but does not present the proposal's causal fixed-signature minimax result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define the logarithmic multiplicities as pole orders of a named real local-zeta/monomial integral, including the rule for chart overlaps and ties, then restate the rate with those invariant quantities.
Replace nearest-resolved-point prose with an explicit measurable selector: metric, chosen lift in each chart, tie-breaking, and a partition-of-unity gluing formula; prove it agrees on overlaps.

Retag frontier-holder as novel or replace it with an original-coordinate smoothness condition, and show how that primitive condition transfers to every certified chart without strengthening the scalar slow-mover literature merely to obtain the rate.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two undefined geometric constructions and the unsupported smoothness tag, then rerun the novelty review; the corrected Hankel-tail/minimax kernel remains flagship-plausible.
